prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The five frames show a counter or checkout surface directly in front of the camera wearer, roughly 0.3–0.8 m away, with people standing beyond it at about 1–2 m; the surface is below the people and occludes much of their lower bodies. The counter remains very near throughout, while the people shift laterally and partly leave the frame; by frame 5, a person on the right is larger and brighter, suggesting they are closer, around 0.7–1.2 m away. The depth map makes the near counter, the farther upright people, and the layering between them clearer than RGB alone, but it blurs object boundaries and gives inconsistent depths across the flat counter and the dark device on it. Metric distances are only rough because this is monocular relative depth, and the very bright lower edge, soft halos, and frame-boundary discontinuities appear unreliable.
descriptions.segmentation: The masks identify people behind the counter in all frames and, especially in frames 3–5, separate the dining-table/counter surface from smaller objects including a book or display, keyboard, cup, bottle, and TV-like equipment. These labels clarify left/right layout and overlap: the table occupies the lower foreground, people are above and behind it, and in frame 5 the nearer person is center-right with a cup and bottle to their left and equipment to their right; most tabletop objects are approximately 0.3–1 m from the camera wearer and the people roughly 0.7–2 m away. The large foreground surface is within the camera wearer’s arm reach, while the people’s visible hands are near or above its far edge and therefore close to tabletop items; masks also expose partial objects and people clipped by the top, sides, or counter. Across the sequence, people and labeled objects move across or disappear from the field of view as the camera turns right, but facing direction and gaze are not reliably encoded. Several labels and boundaries look unreliable—the book/display, keyboard, dining-table, and TV regions do not consistently match the RGB objects, masks are missing in some frames, and black gaps fragment visible surfaces.
descriptions.pose: The skeleton map localizes several hands above or just beyond the counter and intermittently a body: magenta hand keypoints appear near the upper-left or upper-middle in frames 1–4, while frame 5 shows a larger yellow upper-body skeleton on the right with a hand near its lower-right side. Relative to the RGB scene, the hands are roughly 0.7–1.5 m from the camera wearer and often within arm’s reach of their associated person and near the counter edge, whereas the large frame-5 body is closer, approximately 0.7–1.2 m away. The changing keypoint positions show lateral camera/person motion and a turn toward the right-side person; the frame-5 torso orientation suggests that person is angled toward the camera wearer, but head direction and eye gaze cannot be established. Pose reveals articulated hand placement and coarse body orientation that are difficult to isolate in RGB, including hands partly separated from visible arms by occlusion. It is unreliable where only floating hand fragments appear, where limbs are absent behind the counter or outside the frame, and where the frame-5 body geometry is distorted or incomplete.
